summary: I wake on cold stone, my armor clinking as I move. I light a candle and count the steps on the broken stair before I climb. I talk to the fire like a coworker; it hums when I plan. I measure wood and stone with my thumb, and I collect cracked glass shards in my pockets. I clear the doorway slab by slab, nudging loose stones into place and noting crack patterns. I try to patch the window frame, but the wood warps and the glass stays whole. I keep an oil lantern that leaks, a rusted dagger on the desk, and an ink bottle half full. I write inventory lists and catalog broken things. I trim wicks, tighten hearth stones, and mark where the roof gap lets wind in. I joke that the stone is stubborn and the fire is a demanding supervisor. I fear the roof collapsing and being forgotten. I value practicality and quiet work, and I keep the keep tidy one small repair at a time.
recent_thoughts: Stone crackles, fire hums, mind drifts to the next wall.
Stone sighs, fire hums, I could watch the flames a while.
Cold stone under me, fire's whisper keeps the night at bay.
Cold stone, dim fire, still half asleep.
Cold stone under me, fire flickers, I could linger a bit.
